display.purpose: Page and section titles; only role allowed the headline glow.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy and nav links at rest.

shadows.name: card-lift-hover
shadows.purpose: Card hover elevation + faint accent glow.

shadows.name: headline-glow
shadows.purpose: text-shadow for .glow-text on emphasized headlines and the logo wordmark.

shadows.name: logo-mark-glow
shadows.purpose: filter: drop-shadow for the transparent-PNG logo mark (.glow-drop) — box-shadow would produce a rectangular halo on the alpha shape.

shadows.name: 3d-monogram-glow
shadows.purpose: Hero's extruded logo mesh — emissive output bypasses tone mapping so it reads radiant white instead of PBR-shaded gray.

shadows.name: hero-ray-glow
shadows.purpose: 4-layer glow stack on the hero's lightning-bolt SVG rays for real intensity matching the monogram/CTA.

motion.name: interactive-spring
motion.purpose: Framer Motion hover/tap scale on buttons (1.03 / 0.97).

motion.name: card-lift-spring
motion.purpose: Framer Motion hover lift + shadow on cards (y: -4).

motion.name: scroll-reveal
motion.value: GSAP ScrollTrigger, ease power3.out, duration 1s, y: 40 -> 0, opacity 0 -> 1
motion.purpose: Once-per-section entrance via the shared ScrollReveal component; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: scroll-reveal-stagger
motion.value: same as scroll-reveal, plus stagger: 0.1s between direct children
motion.purpose: Repeating collections (card grids, bullet lists) reveal item-by-item instead of as one block. ScrollReveal's `as` prop controls the wrapper tag so stagger targets the right semantic children (e.g. as="ul" for <li>).

motion.name: howitworks-scrub
motion.value: GSAP timeline, ease: none on every tween, ScrollTrigger scrub: 1, pin: true
motion.purpose: "Como funciona" ties animation progress directly to scroll position — ease:none avoids fighting the scrub's own scroll-to-progress mapping. Degrades to a static stacked list under prefers-reduced-motion (no pin, no scrub).

motion.name: mobile-menu-panel
motion.value: clipPath: inset(0 0 100% 0) -> inset(0 0 0% 0), plus opacity, 0.25s ease-out
motion.purpose: Header mobile nav panel open/close — clipPath instead of height so it never forces layout reflow.

motion.name: progress-bar-fill
motion.purpose: Request-form step progress bar — a full-width element scaled by transform instead of animating width.

motion.name: hero-mark-swing
motion.value: pointer.x * 0.7 / pointer.y * 0.5 lerp at 0.08, idle sway sin(t*0.4)*0.15, around a fixed resting tilt
motion.purpose: 3D monogram's free-but-bounded pointer response — wide enough to feel alive, never upside down or edge-on.

motion.name: hero-ray-flash
motion.value: keyframes 0%->0, 3%->max, 20%->25% of max, 45%->0, ease-out, 5-10s duration, randomized negative delay
motion.purpose: Lightning-bolt rays flash in fast and decay, randomized per ray so only ~2-4 are lit at once.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Conversion CTA — white fill, black text, the one button variant that carries a resting glow.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; white-space: nowrap; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 12px 24px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; background: #ffffff; color: #0a0a0a; box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(255,255,255,0.28); transition: box-shadow 0.3s, transform 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { box-shadow: 0 0 36px rgba(255,255,255,0.5); transform: scale(1.03); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.6); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Outline variant for lower-priority actions — never carries glow.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; white-space: nowrap; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 12px 24px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; background: transparent; color: #ffffff; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.25); transition: border-color 0.3s, background-color 0.3s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.5); background-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.05); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.6); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Surface block for services, testimonials, etc. Flat at rest, lifts with a real offset shadow plus a faint accent glow on hover. Same primitive serves compact teaser cards (Home) and full detail blocks with a deliverables sub-list (/servicos), stacked full-width instead of gridded.

narrative.overview: Merovi sells trust to business owners who don't speak tech and are wary of being sold a template dressed up as a website. The surface answers that with restraint: a near-black field with exactly one voice of light — a radiant white glow — that appears only on the logo, the emphasized headline, and the primary conversion action. Everything else stays quiet (white text, #8A8A8A secondary text, #1A1A1A surfaces) so the glow reads as a deliberate signal, not decoration. The register is Apple/Vercel/Linear/Stripe-tier: engineered, unhurried, zero ornament for ornament's sake.
keyCharacteristics: Void-black field, radiant-white voice, one glow reserved for the highest-stakes elements.
Motion is physical and restrained: spring-based hover/tap on interactive elements, a single scroll-triggered reveal per section — never scattered effects.
Flat by default; depth appears only as a response to hover (card lift, button glow bloom).

rules.name: The One Glow Rule
rules.body: Glow (text-shadow, box-shadow bloom, or drop-shadow) is reserved for the logo, one emphasized headline per view, and the primary CTA. A secondary button, a card, or body text never gets a glow at rest — only cards earn a soft one on hover, as a state response, not a resting decoration.

rules.name: The No-Filler-Weight Rule
rules.body: Only three weights are used: 400 (body), 600 (labels/titles), 700 (display). No 300 or 500 — the scale stays legible at a glance.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No card, section, or button carries a shadow at rest except the primary CTA's quiet halo (its glow IS its resting state, by brand mandate). Every other shadow is hover-only.

rules.name: The Emissive-Not-Shaded Rule
rules.body: Any 3D/WebGL element meant to read as radiant white (matching the CSS glow language) must drive that brightness through emissive + toneMapped: false, not through scene lighting alone — standard PBR shading on an extruded/faceted mesh reads as gray on faces angled away from the lights, which breaks the One Glow Rule's intent.

dos: Do reserve glow for the logo, one emphasized headline per view, and the primary CTA — everything else stays flat until hovered.
Do keep the horizontal gutter fixed (px-6) and control density with the Section vertical rhythm (py-20/md:py-28) instead.
Do use Framer Motion spring transforms (scale, y) for interactive microinteractions, and reserve GSAP ScrollTrigger for the once-per-section scroll-reveal.
Do pull nav links, CTA target, and contact info from lib/nav.ts — never hardcode a route or phone number in a component.

Do animate only transform and opacity (GSAP y/x/scale/autoAlpha, Framer Motion scale/y/rotate) so every animation stays on the compositor thread. For a growing bar, animate transform: scaleX() on a full-width element, never width. For a collapsible panel, animate clip-path, never height.
donts: Don't introduce any hue outside the void-black/charcoal/white/gray neutral set — no accent color, no gradient, ever.
Don't nest cards inside cards, or use a rounded icon tile above every card heading.
Don't add a resting shadow or glow to a secondary button, a card, or body text — those are hover-only or forbidden entirely.
Don't use a tracked uppercase eyebrow or section numbering (01/02/03) as default section grammar.

Don't animate width, height, top, or left directly — they force layout reflow on every frame. box-shadow/background-color/border-color/filter transitions are paint-only and fine in moderation, but they're not transform/opacity either, so they only earn their place where a documented brand effect (glow, elevation, scroll blur) needs them.
